grounds.alternatives: strip, widened by a family's own documentation: asyncio, anyio and trio (flake8-async); typing and typing_extensions (typing_extensions); Crypto and Cryptodome (pycryptodome)
grounds.blacklist: bandit's blacklist data: the top-level package of each qualname; [] for B4xx, which bandit also checks on Call, where __import__ needs no import
grounds.declared: bandit's own @checks declaration: the node types the test reads; FunctionDef sits on a scope, every other node inside a statement
grounds.docs: the tool's own documentation, quoted in the key's note
grounds.example: each finding of the rule on its own published faulty example: the deepest node holding the finding's span and the nodes holding it, up to the nearest statement
grounds.example+docs: example, widened by the Python documentation: ast 'AsyncFunctionDef ... Has the same fields as FunctionDef.'; 'AsyncFor ... AsyncWith ... They have the same fields as For and With, respectively.'; 'TryStar ... The attributes are the same as for Try'; and the language reference 7.11, import_stmt: "import" module ... | "from" relative_module "import"
grounds.kinds: the example written as <name>.py, test_<name>.py, <name>.pyi and a one-cell <name>.ipynb: the kinds where the rule fires
grounds.paths: the semgrep rule's own languages and paths.include
grounds.scope: the tool's own scope: it reads the project to give a finding
grounds.strip: the example with each import statement replaced by pass: [] when the rule still fires, else the modules whose single removal lowers its findings, checked by removing only them
grounds.unparse: the rule fires on its example and is silent on ast.unparse of the same AST, so it reads text the AST does not hold and fits any input holding that line

keys.file: the file kinds the rule reads, of source, test, stub, notebook
keys.imports: the top-level modules an input's file must import one of; [] for none
keys.nodes: the AST node types an input must hold one of for the rule to have a subject
keys.reach: the smallest input a finding of the rule fits inside, of statement, scope, module, project

card.open: a key the measurement cannot ground carries open and its reason, and binds nothing; --proof opens each key that a proof on src/ shows leaving out a real finding, naming the input

sources.bandit: git clone --depth 1 --branch 1.9.4 --filter=blob:none --sparse https://github.com/PyCQA/bandit.git bandit; git -C bandit sparse-checkout set examples
sources.mypy: the python blocks under each '.. _code-<code>:' section of docs/source/error_code_list.rst and error_code_list2.rst at https://github.com/python/mypy/tree/v2.1.0, saved under mypy_docs/
sources.ruff: python -m ruff rule --all --output-format json: the blocks of each page's '## Example' section above its 'Use instead' line, the first one read
sources.semgrep: git clone --depth 1 --filter=blob:none --sparse https://github.com/semgrep/semgrep-rules.git; git -C semgrep-rules sparse-checkout set python generic; the rules saved from https://semgrep.dev/c/p/python and https://semgrep.dev/c/p/security-audit as p_python.yaml and p_security-audit.yaml
